Many members of the current anti-AI crowd will use AI in the future. The writers I know personally, who are anti-AI, have done little or no research on AI, and have not experimented with AI. Their biggest resentment is that new writers using AI will not have to go through the same learning curves and struggles they had to endure to create a novel, but what they really fear most is the vast number of books AI can generate in a shorter period of time.

Overcoming a discoverability problem is not significantly easier whether there are four million titles or ten million titles available. The percentage of writers using AI to assist in their writing will continue to grow. Younger writers are more inclined to adapt new technologies quicker than older writers.

Experienced writers, who already know have to craft a compelling story, are more likely to be successful using AI as an assistant than are new writers who have never written a story. Simply prompting AI to write a mystery novel typically creates a less than desirable result.

The number of writers using AI for book cover designs will continue to grow. Anyone thinking traditional publishers will not use AI to reduce their operating costs should think again. History shows us that any new technology that reduces the operating costs of a business eventually gets adopted by those businesses.
